facts.label: Entrar no show
facts.sub: Na porta do teatro, o lanterninha confere os ingressos e diz a fileira. Mostre, agradeça e pergunte onde fica.

facts.label: Ingresso no celular
facts.sub: Muitos teatros escaneiam um código QR no celular. Deixe a tela com brilho alto e a bateria carregada, e tenha o ingresso aberto antes de chegar à porta. Se der problema, o lanterninha ajuda: “Can you help me, please?”

facts.label: Chegue cedo
facts.sub: Em muitos shows as portas abrem antes do início. Chegar com folga ajuda a comprar bebida, achar a fileira e evitar fila. Normalmente quem chega depois que o show começa espera um momento certo para entrar.

compare.br: In Brazil, many theaters and shows ask people to arrive early, and the ticket often has a seat number too. Some places ask you to silence your phone.
compare.us: In the USA an usher often checks your ticket and points to your row. People arrive early, buy a drink or program, and clap at the end.
compare.tip: If you cannot find your seat, ask the usher: “Where is row ten?” They answer this question all night.

pages.title: A sold-out night in Las Vegas · 1/3
paragraphs: Mia and her brother Leo come to a big theater in **Las Vegas**. The lights outside are very bright. A sign says **SOLD OUT**. The tickets were selling like hotcakes!

A man in a black jacket smiles at them. His name is Isaac, and he is an usher. “Hello! **Are you here for the show?**” he asks. “Yes. **We have two tickets**,” Mia says. “**May I see them?**” Isaac asks. Mia opens her phone and says, “**Here you go.**”

pages.title: A sold-out night in Las Vegas · 2/3
paragraphs: Isaac checks the code on the phone. “Your seats are in **row ten**,” he says. “Thank you. **Where is that?**” Leo asks. “**Down the aisle, on the left**,” Isaac answers. Small lights on the floor show the way.

Leo is thirsty and the show starts in ten minutes. “**Can we buy a drink first?**” he asks. “Yes, **the bar is over there**,” Isaac says. Mia gets water and Leo gets a soda. They also buy a program for five dollars.

pages.title: Laboratório de sons · o som
pages.what: Em inglês, o ritmo vem das palavras de conteúdo (seats, row, ten), que são longas e fortes. As pequenas (are, in, the) ficam rápidas e fracas. Quem fala tudo com a mesma força soa cansativo.
pages.how: Bata a mesa só nas palavras fortes: SEATS · ROW · TEN. Diga as fracas bem rápido, quase engolidas, entre uma batida e outra. Mantenha o tempo igual entre as batidas.
